game.name: Halls of Torment
game.short_description: Slay hordes of terrifying monsters in this horde survival roguelite. Descend into the Halls of Torment where the Lords of the underworld await you. Treasures, magical trinkets, and a growing cast of heroes will grant you the power to vanquish these horrors from beyond. How long can you survive?

commentary.label: Tier list Part 3 (2025)
commentary.summary: Halls of Torment is a horde-survivor roguelike with a dark, old-school Diablo look. It keeps core gameplay simple and instead leans on exploration, a huge amount of unlockables, and a strong sense of progression. He compares the early hours to first playing Vampire Survivors. Drawbacks are poor UI and stat explanations, limited replayability once everything is seen, and too little content per level. His main complaint is simply wanting more, and he places it in A tier.
praise: Visuals evoke classic Diablo and have a unique charm
Massive amount of unlockables, with achievement boards per character and general boards
First few hours of progression feel amazing, like early Vampire Survivors
Each new level looks different with new enemies, bosses, characters and abilities
Hidden quests in levels (find a tome, follow a blood trail) reward exploration, e.g. boss damage and unlocks
Abilities are cool and some unique; upgrading then evolving them feels great
Infinite borderless level layouts encourage exploring
criticism: Game explains itself terribly; UI is bad, e.g. keyword 'force' needs multiple clicks and stays confusing
Stat explanations barely matter since most picks are generally good
Less replayable than other horde-likes once all levels, bosses and abilities are seen
Only one unique quest per level, which disappointed him once he knew
Wants more unique things to find, more bosses and more levels
unique_points: Doesn't innovate on mechanics; focuses on overall experience, exploration and progression instead
In-run quests narrated by a voice tie exploration to boss damage and unlocks
Unlock-driven structure where progress is constant, with thousands of things to unlock
commentary.quote: very, very solid HordeLike, very simple in concept with wonderful visuals
design_criteria: Meta-progression/unlockables: huge unlock count and achievement boards drive motivation
Level design: infinite open layouts with distinct looks per level and hidden quests
Visuals/charm: Diablo-inspired look is a major draw
Enemy/boss variety: new enemies and bosses per level are a highlight
Ability design: unique abilities with upgrade and evolution paths
UI/clarity: poor explanation of stats and keywords hurts it
Replayability: drops off after content is exhausted
Content volume: wants more quests, bosses and levels

commentary.label: Top 10 of 2024 (#10)
commentary.summary: Halls of Torment is a top-down bullet heaven (which he calls a 'horde-like') with simple controls: move and occasionally aim abilities. He calls it one of the best horde-likes of the year even though it is less unique than other games on his list. Its Diablo 1 style look and hack-and-slash feel are a highlight. His verdict is a solid pick for anyone wanting a simple take that recaptures some of the Vampire Survivors thrill.
praise: Aesthetics and hack-and-slash gameplay reminiscent of Diablo 1
Unique equipment that opens up many possible builds
Pacing is the best part: constant reward from new maps, secrets, characters and achievements in early hours
Every run feels rewarding and keeps him engaged
criticism: Gameplay is a bit more repetitive than Vampire Survivors
Wants more secrets and late-game content such as extra encounters or events during runs
User interface and information given to players are weak; stats are hard to understand
unique_points: Not especially unique in a crowded genre, but stands out through polish and reward pacing
Early-game discovery loop of maps, secrets and characters keeps runs feeling rewarding
commentary.quote: Halls of Torment is one of the best Horde likes of the year
design_criteria: Pacing: constant reward and discovery in early hours
Aesthetics: Diablo 1 inspired look and feel
Build variety: unique equipment enabling many builds
Content depth: wants more late-game secrets and events
UI/information clarity: stats hard to understand
Repetition: somewhat more repetitive than Vampire Survivors
Meta-progression: achievements and unlocks drive engagement

community.one_liner: A Diablo 1/2-styled horde-survival (Vampire Survivors-like) action roguelite with pre-rendered retro art, from Chasing Carrots (Stuttgart), where you pick a hero, auto-fire abilities into huge mobs and fight a timed ~30-minute run to a boss.
community.consensus_summary: Halls of Torment is rated Overwhelmingly Positive on Steam (about 95% of roughly 31.9k reviews) and scores 88 on Metacritic from 8 critics (user score 7.6). Critics and players alike treat it as one of the best Vampire Survivors-likes, mostly on the strength of its Diablo-era atmosphere, build variety and deep meta-progression, though several note it does not reinvent the genre. It was in Early Access from May 2023 (70k+ sales in week one) and had its 1.0 release on Sep 24, 2024; it is still being updated (Boglands DLC Nov 2025, a free Archives preview-update series running through Sep 2026). Recent reviews are a bit cooler (about 83% positive over the last 30 days in one snapshot), driven by stability complaints on high Agony difficulties and by fatigue with fixed-length runs.
best_things: Diablo 1/2 pre-rendered pixel aesthetic, gothic atmosphere and music nail late-90s ARPG nostalgia; PC Gamer and many Steam reviewers single this out
Large hero roster with distinct playstyles plus a huge pool of traits, abilities and items (reviewers cite 1,000+ traits, 60 items, hundreds of rare variants) gives real build variety
Deep meta-progression and unlocks (maps, heroes, quests, Agony difficulty tiers) keep the 'one more run' loop going for hundreds of hours
Excellent value: usually under $10, and several players report 100-300+ hours
Satisfying power fantasy as builds snowball and the screen fills with effects; ARPG-style itemisation and loot feel instead of only passive upgrades
Polished quest/achievement tracker (500 achievements) that gives clear goals; one reviewer calls it the best tracker they have seen
Actively supported developer: years of free updates, paid but well-received DLC, plus mobile (Oct 2024) and PS5/Xbox (Oct 2025) ports
worst_things: Fixed ~25-30 minute runs: the first ~10 minutes are busy, then long stretches of low-decision autopilot waiting for the boss timer; many negative reviews cite boredom here

Crashes and performance problems in late-game/high Agony content with massive hordes, especially certain abilities (for example Avalanche) and the Boglands map; also reported on Steam Deck and Linux despite 'Verified' status
Buildcraft and map design can feel samey: some players say unlocking all maps/heroes changes little, and Ars Technica (per Wikipedia) noted levels lack distinct identity
Does not innovate beyond the Vampire Survivors formula; several critics and positive reviewers say so
Some achievements depend on rare RNG spawns/events that may not appear, turning completion into waiting
Missing quality-of-life options: no game-speed or run-length toggle, no save-and-resume mid run, no mute when unfocused (per one reviewer)
Sparse 'dopamine drip' feel: one reviewer said it made them hyper-aware of time spent and they walked away
Some reviewers find the game slow and primitive early on: few skills, several heroes feel alike, and some characters are noticeably weaker than others
improvements: Add run-length options, a speed-up/turbo toggle, or save-and-return so the 30-minute loop is less of a commitment
Fix stability and memory issues at Agony 3+ and in the Bog before shipping more content (a recurring 'fix crashes first' request on Steam)
Make achievements less RNG-dependent so quests/spawns reliably appear
Increase decision density mid-run (more mid-run choices, events, more differentiated maps) to cut the autopilot stretch
Add audio option to mute when the window is not in focus and general QoL settings
Make buildcraft more exciting / make hero and map unlocks change gameplay more meaningfully
unique_things: Fully Diablo-flavoured presentation: pre-rendered sprites, ARPG loot vocabulary, dark fantasy underworld framing and 'Lords' as bosses
Creative director's pitch: Diablo as a three-course meal, this as the candy bar; it plays like a compressed ARPG instead of an arcade score-chaser
Very deep trait/item/rare-variant system and a 500-quest progression layer on top of the usual survivors loop
Timed structure with a mid-run boss spawn and a 30-minute main boss, closer to a Diablo act structure than endless survival
Built in the open-source Godot engine after the team moved away from Unity; five-person studio and a cheap ($6.66) price point
tedious_or_disliked: Long stretches of standing and auto-attacking after the map is cleared, waiting for the 30-minute boss
Grinding the 500 achievements, especially those tied to rare enemies or events that refuse to spawn
Crash-induced loss of progress and the need to avoid certain abilities or maps to stay stable at high difficulty
Unlock treadmill where heroes/maps unlocked late do not noticeably change how runs play
Level-up and item pause screens stretch the nominal 30-minute run to roughly 40 real minutes, with no suspend option
divisive_points: Run length: some love 30 minutes as a satisfying build-up to a boss, others find it far too long for this genre
Depth vs sameness: fans say it has enormous depth if you dig down, critics of it say builds and maps blur together
Innovation: 'best in genre execution' versus 'nothing new beyond Vampire Survivors'
Value of the Boglands DLC and the post-launch updates: praised by many, but one reviewer reported game-breaking bugs two weeks after the DLC launch
community.reception_notes: Early Access launched May 24, 2023 with 70k+ units in week one; 1.0 launched Sep 24, 2024 with peak concurrents since Aug 2023, and 1M+ Steam sales by Oct 2024. Steam Revenue Calculator estimates about $7.0M gross and about $2.1M net (Boxleiter-based, order-of-magnitude only). Nominated for Mobile Game of the Year at the 28th D.I.C.E. Awards. Mobile ports Oct 2024 (Erabit Studios) and PS5/Xbox Oct 2025. Boglands DLC arrived with the Nov 2025 Bog update, and a free 'Archives' preview update series ran from Mar 2026 through Sep 28, 2026; fix patches for crashes and resource leaks shipped Nov 2025 and Apr 2026, though some recent reviews still report crashes at Agony 3+ and Steam Deck issues. The Steam forum keeps a pinned known-issues thread and the crash/technical topics dominate player discussion. Windows and Linux on Steam, no Mac.
